adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:77 — group.save` after `group.add` is a no-op that returns true (adds already committed via the association), so the success/error branch verifies nothing and a partially-applied add can still report success or, conversely, error after members were persisted

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` (and similarly `#remove_member`), the code mutates membership via `group.add(user)` / `group.users.delete(user_id)` inside the loop and only afterwards calls `group.save` to decide whether to render success vs error. In Rails/Discourse, association mutations like these typically persist immediately (and the previous implementation in this same controller did not call `group.save` at all when adding/removing members, implying `group.add/remove` already commit changes). That makes the subsequent `group.save` largely unrelated to whether member adds/removals succeeded, and it can also report an error after membership changes have already been applied (no transaction/rollback), leading to inconsistent API semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — group.users.delete(id)` on a has_many-through issues `delete_all` on the join table, skipping GroupUser destroy callbacks/counter_cache so `user_count` drifts upward permanently after every removal

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — Rails resolves the integer via `association.find(id)`, so removing a non-member (double click, concurrent removal by two admins, stale UI) raises RecordNotFound instead of being idempotent

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` where `user_id` is an Integer from params. For a `has_many`/`has_many :through` collection, passing an Integer to `collection.delete` causes Rails to resolve it via the association scope (effectively `group.users.find(user_id)` before deleting). If the user exists but is not currently a member (double-click/concurrent removal/stale UI), that lookup can raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`, making the endpoint non-idempotent and potentially returning an error instead of a success no-op. This is directly implied by the diff’s use of an Integer id rather than a member record.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — usernames.split(",")` blows up with NoMethodError (500) when a client sends `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` or a hash, since `params.require` returns the raw Array/Hash

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then immediately calls `usernames.split(",")`. If a client submits `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`, Rails will parse `params[:usernames]` as an `Array` (and a hash would remain a `Hash`), and `params.require(:usernames)` will return that raw object. `Array`/`Hash` do not respond to `split`, so this would raise `NoMethodError` and result in a 500. The diff does not coerce or validate `usernames` to a String before calling `split`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — Unknown usernames are skipped silently and the endpoint still returns success_json, so the UI reports "added" when zero members were added and no test covers it

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does skip unknown usernames (`User.find_by_username` returning nil just does nothing) and still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds. However, this behavior is not clearly a defect introduced by the diff: the previous implementation for incremental membership updates explicitly had a test asserting it “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users,” suggesting silent skipping was intended. Also, the claim that “the UI reports 'added'” is not verifiable from this diff (the JS `addMembers` action does not display a success message here). The “no test covers it” part is true, but missing test coverage alone is not a concrete bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38 — group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` runs unconditionally, so any update omitting `visible` silently flips the group to not visible

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Admin::GroupsController#update`, `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` is executed unconditionally. In Ruby, if `params[:visible]` is omitted (nil), the expression evaluates to `false`, so any update request that doesn’t include `visible` will flip an otherwise-visible group to `false`. There is no `if params[:visible].present?` guard like there is for `alias_level`, so this is a real correctness bug in the updated code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22 — create` ignores `alias_level` although the client's `asJSON` sends it, so a newly created group silently loses the chosen alias level and no spec checks it

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the client now POSTs group data via `Discourse.Group#create()` using `asJSON()`, which includes `alias_level` (`asJSON` returns `{ name, alias_level, visible }`). However, `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `group.name` and `group.visible` and never reads/sets `params[:alias_level]`. This means any non-default alias level selected in the UI will be silently dropped on creation (group will keep model/default alias_level). The updated specs for `.create` only check name stripping and do not cover alias_level, so this regression would go untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:23 — params[:offset].to_i` accepts negative values and passes them straight to `.offset()`, producing a Postgres error / 500 on `?offset=-1

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then uses it directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. If the request provides `?offset=-1`, `to_i` yields `-1` and Rails will generate SQL with `OFFSET -1`, which Postgres rejects ("OFFSET must not be negative"), causing a 500. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23 — offset is clamped against the stale client-side user_count, so after removing the last member on the last page the refetch returns an empty page

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:94 — Automatic-group guard tests hardcode group_id/id 1 and rely on a seeded automatic group instead of Fabricate(:group, automatic: true), so the 422 could come from an unrelated cause
